In addition to providing public comment in person at the meeting, the following opportunity has been
established:

Public Comments

Please email all public comments to HEARCommission@sgch.org and include the following on the subject
line of your email: the section (Public Comment, New Business, Staff Items) and Item Number you are
commenting on. Staff will read public comments into the record for up to the three-minute limit. Words
that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be
read. All public comments shall be emailed by 5:00 P.M. on meeting day.

Watch the Meeting Online
Live broadcasts of the meetings are available using the following link:

https://www.youtube.com/CityofSanGabriel

  Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, June 28, 2022

 Purpose of the Commission: The purpose of the HEAR Commission is to advance and advocate
 for equity, access, diversity, social justice, safety, mutual appreciation, increased cultural
 competency, positive inter-group relations and respect for all members of the San Gabriel
 community (the “Purpose”).

    PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Commissioner Khan

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the HEAR Commission

  1. Minutes of the HEAR Commission Regular Meeting on May 24, 2022.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. DISCUSSION OF APPROVED 2022 ANNUAL WORKPLAN

  Commission members to continue working on the approved 2022 Annual Workplan.
  The Workplan items of primary focus include: Item 2a- Develop and implement
  programs and events- More specifically the San Gabriel Mental Health Expo and Item
  2c- Guest Speakers.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the HEAR Commission continue working on the 2022 Annual

  Each Commissioner may address the HEAR Commission and public on matters of general

   MINUTES OF TUESDAY, MAY 24, 2022
  MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS, AND RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Jennings-Nuñez called the regular meeting of the HEAR Commission to order at 6:36 p.m.
on Tuesday, May 24, 2022, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San
Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Herrera.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Jacqueline Borja, Susan Fitzsimmons, Viki Goto, Jorge Herrera,
  Chasity Jennings-Nuñez, and Riaz (Rick) Khan

Commissioners Absent:  Michelle Brenhaug

ANNOUNCMENTS

Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager, provided information for the public on
how to submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the HEAR
Commission, e-mail all public comments to HEARCommission@sgch.org.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez hearing no objections, the Agenda Order was approved.

  2. PUBLIC COMMENT

  None

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  May 24, 2022
   3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  A motion was made by Commissioner Khan and seconded by Vice-Chair Goto to
  approve the minutes of the HEAR Commission Regular Meeting for April 26, 2022.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 6-0-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Borja, Fitzsimmons, Goto, Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez, Khan
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None
  Absent: Brenhaug

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. DISCUSSION OF APPROVED 2022 ANNUAL WORKPLAN

  Manager Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager, presented an update for
  the Commission to review. The Commission discussed the Engagement Survey
  results, reviewed the upcoming speaker list, and discussed details for the San
  Gabriel Mental Health and Wellness Expo on September 18, 2022. Commissioner
  Herrera recognized Recreation Leaders, Hailey Villalobos and Sarah Reyes, for their
  hard work assisting Cinco de Mayo participants with Engagement Survey
  submissions.

  A motion was made by Vice-Chair Goto and seconded by Commissioner Borja to
  schedule the presentations for the list provided with June being a representative
  for acknowledgement of Pride Month.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 6-0-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Borja, Fitzsimmons, Goto, Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez, Khan
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None
  Absent: Brenhaug

  Public Comment: None

  *Technical difficulties 7:03pm

  B. LAND ACKNOWLEDGMENT STATEMENT

  Manager Morales-Stevens presented that the Land Acknowledgment Statement
  Committee had two individual meetings with Chief Morales and Chief Salas. Staff
  will provide a full report for the Commission to review at a later date.

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  May 24, 2022
   Chair Jennings-Nuñez shared the purpose of the Land Acknowledgment
  Statement. “The Land Acknowledgement Statement serves as a clear and ongoing
  commitment from the City of San Gabriel to respect and acknowledge the native
  peoples of San Gabriel for their past, present, and future contributions to the
  region.”

  5. COMMISSION REPORTS

  Commissioner Khan reported that he attended the City of San Gabriel’s Annual
  Play Day on May 21.

  Commissioner Herrera attended the Cinco de Mayo event and shared the
  heartwarming experience of diversity. He strongly encourages the community to
  attend meetings and submit comments to the HEAR Commission.

  Commissioner Goto reported that there was a mass shooting in Uvalde, Texas on
  May 24. Goto reported that there have been 210 Mass shootings in the U.S this
  year. She shared Facing History & Ourselves which have resources on how to talk
  to children about tragic events (facinghistory.org). Goto invited the public to attend
  the following live theatre events:
   East-West Players in Downtown Los Angeles is presenting “Interstate,” a
  new musical by Kit Yan and Melissa li June 2 – 22 (eastwestplayers.org).
   Sierra Madre playhouse presenting the King of Yees May 20- June 12
  (sierramadreplayhouse.org).

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez attended Block the Hate which was sponsored by
  Compassion SGV at Vincent Lugo Park. She reported that May is Mental Health
  Awareness Month and urges the community to investigate resources. Chair
  Jennings-Nuñez also highlighted that June is Pride Month and June 19th is
  Juneteenth. Chair Jennings-Nuñez invited the community to Pasadena Jackie
  Robinson Community Center’s Juneteenth Celebration on Saturday, June 18.

  Commissioner Fitzsimmons attended the Brown Act and Ethics Training hosted by
  the City Clerk’s Office.

  Commissioner Borja attended the Cinco de Mayo event and shared that it was
  enjoyable event.

  6. STAFF COMMENTS

  Community Services Director, Rebecca Perez announced that Matthew Morales-
  Stevens’ has been promoted to the position of Community Services Manager.

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  May 24, 2022
   7. ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez adjourned the meeting at 7:57 p.m.

  Next regular meeting is tentatively scheduled in person for Tuesday, June 28, 2022 at 6:30
  p.m.

Respectfully submitted:

_______________________________________________
Danielle Adriano, Recreation Specialist
